story.head: Who blinks first?
paras: The Avalanche have won two in a row, while the Red Wings (6-5-3) lost 5-4 to St. Louis on Oct 31. Going in, the Wings are last in the Atlantic (tied for 19th in the NHL) and the Avalanche third in the Central (tied for 13th).

The Red Wings have played better than their record (.536) says: their chances are worth about .620, and their finishing has held them back. The Avalanche’s record (.607) is about what their chances are worth.

The Red Wings block more shots than almost anyone (2nd) and draw more penalties than they take (3rd), but ice the puck a lot (30th). The Avalanche do a lot of their shooting from distance (lowest) and play the league’s fastest games (1st). They also get their defensemen shooting (2nd), so their defensemen shoot a lot, and the Red Wings’ not so much. Colorado has scored 4.21 goals a game, the most in the league. The Red Wings’ power play against the Avalanche’s penalty killers is strength against strength.

Alex DeBrincat (6 G / 9 A / 15 P in 14 GP) leads the Red Wings in scoring. Viktor Arvidsson (8 G / 6 A / 14 P in 14 GP) has a team-high eight goals, with eight points in his last five games. Nathan MacKinnon (9 G / 15 A / 24 P in 14 GP) leads the Avalanche in scoring and is tied for fourth in the NHL, with eight points in his last five games and five goals in six games against Detroit since 2023-24. Artturi Lehkonen (12 G / 5 A / 17 P in 14 GP) has a team-high twelve goals, tied for second in the NHL, with eight points in his last five games.
John Gibson (4-5-1 / .860 SV% in 10 GS) has had a rough start to the season for Detroit, but will likely start. Mackenzie Blackwood (7-3-0 / .897 SV% in 10 GS) is in line to start for Colorado.
The Avalanche usually control more of the chances than the Red Wings do.

items.text: The Red Wings are newly without Dylan Larkin, and have been without Marco Kasper, Jacob Bernard-Docker and Mason Appleton for several games.
With Dylan Larkin out, Emmitt Finnie took twelve faceoffs in the Red Wings’ last game. He had been taking about three a game.
Artturi Lehkonen has twelve goals on chances worth about 5.2 goals, well above what his finishing usually turns chances into. Runs like that tend to cool off.
Nathan MacKinnon and Devon Toews have a point in four straight games.
